qualifying_findings.title: Zscaler MCP Server fixed HMAC confirmation tokens not bound to target resources
qualifying_findings.evidence_classification: CVE Program and NVD vulnerability records with upstream repository pull request reference
qualifying_findings.summary: Zscaler MCP Server confirmation tokens were HMAC-protected but not bound to the target resource identifier. An MCP client or agent could replay a token generated for one resource against another resource of the same type, crossing the intended confirmation boundary.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: MCP tools often use confirmation tokens as delegated-action safety gates. Tokens that are not resource-bound can turn user confirmation for one action into authority over a different action.

upstream_routing.security_local: Keep the resource-bound confirmation-token flaw, affected MCP action boundary, and 0.7.2 mitigation here.
upstream_routing.ai_wiki: Zscaler and the MCP server as broad ecosystem entities belong upstream if durable product coverage is needed.
upstream_routing.ai_dev_wiki: General MCP confirmation UX and agent workflow practice belong upstream unless framed as this security control.

qualifying_findings.confidence_notes: High confidence from CVE Program and NVD timestamps in-window. Repository PR reference should be rechecked during ingest for exact patch mechanics.

qualifying_findings.title: fast-mcp-telegram patched exfiltrating SSRF in MCP file URL downloads
qualifying_findings.evidence_classification: CVE Program and NVD vulnerability records with GitHub advisory, patch commit, and release references
qualifying_findings.affected_boundary_or_version: fast-mcp-telegram versions before 30.1; fixed in 30.1 / release tag 0.30.1.
qualifying_findings.summary: The Telegram MCP server accepted HTTP(S) URLs for files passed to send_message and send_message_to_phone. Its _validate_url_security denylist checked only the literal hostname string and did not resolve DNS before httpx fetched the target, so a hostname resolving to loopback, private, link-local, or metadata IPs could pass validation. Because the fetched body was returned as a Telegram attachment, the SSRF was exfiltrating rather than blind.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: MCP messaging tools can become network egress and data-exfiltration bridges when tool inputs trigger server-side fetches. DNS-aware egress pinning is required at dial time, not only at URL-parse time.

upstream_routing.security_local: Keep the SSRF, egress validation, exfiltration, and fixed-version detail here.
upstream_routing.ai_wiki: The MCP server entity and Telegram integration background belong upstream if needed.
upstream_routing.ai_dev_wiki: General agent messaging workflow practice belongs upstream unless tied to SSRF prevention controls.

qualifying_findings.confidence_notes: High confidence from CVE Program, NVD, and GitHub advisory references. Ingest should reconcile the version spelling difference between CVE '< 30.1' and GitHub release tag '0.30.1'.

qualifying_findings.title: Token Optimizer MCP patched unauthenticated dashboard log traversal and smart_user command injection
qualifying_findings.evidence_classification: CVE Program and NVD vulnerability records with GitHub advisories, patch commit, and fixed release reference
qualifying_findings.summary: Token Optimizer MCP exposed dashboard session-summary and session-events endpoints without authentication and joined caller-controlled sessionId values into filesystem paths, allowing unauthenticated reads of reachable .jsonl files. A second CVE covered OS command injection in the smart_user tool, where an MCP client that could call get-user-info could execute shell commands through the username argument as the token-optimizer-mcp server user.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: The product stores and serves coding-agent session telemetry and live knowledge-graph context. Unauthenticated log traversal exposes prompts, events, and local session traces, while command injection in an MCP tool converts delegated context optimization into host command execution.

upstream_routing.security_local: Keep the unauthenticated dashboard path traversal, session-log exposure, command injection, and v5.1.0 mitigation here.
upstream_routing.ai_wiki: Token Optimizer MCP as a product/entity belongs upstream if broad catalog coverage is needed.
upstream_routing.ai_dev_wiki: General coding-agent context optimization practice belongs upstream; this repository owns the security failure modes.

qualifying_findings.confidence_notes: High confidence from two in-window CVE publications and matching GitHub advisory references.

qualifying_findings.title: Tencent AI-Infra-Guard disclosed File Access path traversal in dir_actions.py
qualifying_findings.evidence_classification: CVE Program and NVD vulnerability records with VulDB and upstream issue, pull request, commit, and release references
qualifying_findings.affected_boundary_or_version: Tencent AI-Infra-Guard 4.5.0, 4.5.1, 4.5.2, 4.6.1, and 4.6.2 are listed as affected; CVE data also lists 4.6.0 inconsistently as both affected and unaffected. NVD says versions up to 4.5.2/4.6.2 and upgrade to 4.6.0 mitigates.
qualifying_findings.summary: Tencent AI-Infra-Guard's File Access component in skill_scan/tools/dir/dir_actions.py used startsWith-style path validation that allowed local path traversal. The exploit was listed as public, with references to a GitHub issue, pull request, patch commit, and release.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: AI infrastructure scanning tools often inspect project, model, and deployment artifacts. A file-access path traversal inside a security scanner can break the expected repository/artifact boundary and expose local files to an attacker with local or tool-invocation access.

upstream_routing.security_local: Keep the scanner file-access traversal, local boundary, and version reconciliation follow-up here.
upstream_routing.ai_wiki: Tencent and AI-Infra-Guard as broad AI/security tool entities belong upstream if needed.
upstream_routing.ai_dev_wiki: General scanner usage and development workflow guidance belongs upstream unless tied to scanner trust boundaries.

qualifying_findings.confidence_notes: Medium-high confidence. The CVE and NVD records are in-window and concrete, but affected/fixed version fields conflict and require ingest-time reconciliation against the release and patch.

qualifying_findings.title: agentverus-scanner disclosed untrusted-input reliance in security-defense classification
qualifying_findings.evidence_classification: CVE Program and NVD vulnerability records with VulDB and upstream issue references
qualifying_findings.affected_boundary_or_version: agentverus-scanner 0.8.0 and 0.8.1; no fixed version identified in the CVE record.
qualifying_findings.summary: agentverus-scanner's dist/scanner/analyzers/context.js isSecurityDefenseSkill path was reported to rely on untrusted inputs in a security decision. The NVD record says exploitation is local, public exploit information exists, and the project had not responded at publication time.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: AI or agent security scanners must not let analyzed content or local untrusted inputs influence security-defense classification decisions. A scanner that trusts the subject being scanned can create false assurance or suppress findings.

upstream_routing.security_local: Keep the scanner trust-boundary and assurance implication here.
upstream_routing.ai_wiki: agentverus as a product/entity belongs upstream if broad ecosystem coverage is needed.
upstream_routing.ai_dev_wiki: General scanner integration practice belongs upstream unless tied to assurance control failure.
